source_title: OECD AI and the future of social protection
unit_or_scope: OECD social programs and AI use cases
direct_observation: Current AI uses center on client support back-office automation and fraud detection while future uses include outreach early intervention and tailored support with privacy error and trust risks
closed_stage: use-case map and governance risk boundary
missing_stage: claimant exposure subgroup accuracy non-take-up notice correction and benefit receipt
next_test: trace one use case from model or automation to claimant review appeal and payment

source_title: OECD Harnessing AI in Social Security
direct_observation: AI is explored for eligibility checks document processing and service delivery and Catalonia has a named energy-poverty eligibility-reporting use case
missing_stage: household enrollment payment continuity false positives and negatives explanation and remedy
next_test: audit Catalonia or another named system for eligibility accuracy notice correction and payment continuity

source_title: OECD Using AI to manage minimum-income benefits and unemployment assistance
direct_observation: AI may improve timeliness and take-up but may produce biased eligibility assessments or increase inequality across information eligibility and undue-payment detection
missing_stage: named performance claimant understanding appeal correction and material outcome
next_test: compare model-assisted and human-only cases by subgroup and outcome

unit_or_scope: public authorities deciding essential benefits and services
direct_observation: AI granting denying reducing revoking or reclaiming essential benefits can affect livelihood and fundamental rights and is high-risk
closed_stage: legal risk classification and accountability baseline
missing_stage: compliance deployment inventory notice human review appeal and payment continuity
next_test: obtain a deployment inventory and verify logs oversight notices and appeal records

direct_observation: Fewer than one in three feel they could easily receive benefits if needed 40 percent view AI-assisted processing as good for users and 32 percent trust government with collected data
missing_stage: actual service experience automation effect on excluded groups and claimant outcomes
next_test: link survey perceptions to administrative completion appeal and payment data by subgroup

source_title: UK Universal Credit Advances machine-learning model effectiveness assessment
unit_or_scope: Universal Credit advance requests and fraud-prevention interventions April 2025-March 2026
direct_observation: DWP reports a live model prioritizes advance requests for fraud-prevention intervention and a human reviews evidence and decides; the analysis is experimental and iterative
closed_stage: named deployment human-review safeguard and evaluation boundary
missing_stage: false-positive and false-negative claimant rates subgroup fairness intervention burden payment delay hardship appeal and fraud avoided
next_test: link model flag intervention notice decision payment timing and claimant appeal

source_title: Australian National Audit Office AI and Medicare Benefits Integrity
unit_or_scope: Australian Medicare Benefits Integrity Division provider claims and fraud detection
direct_observation: ANAO reports irregular monitoring absent fairness or bias metrics and 22 percent accuracy for one AI-enabled model analysis; AI model use ended in December 2025 in favor of logistic regression while future AI use was considered
closed_stage: named performance governance deficiency and model substitution
missing_stage: claimant or provider consequence subgroup distribution recovered money wrongful suspicion remedy and outcome
next_test: trace model selection manual review payment consequence and correction by provider subgroup

source_title: EU AI Act Service Desk essential services
unit_or_scope: EU public administrations social housing unemployment and essential benefits
direct_observation: EU examples classify eligibility scoring and fraud or dependency prediction using demographic behavioural and financial data as high-risk and identify some benefit-fraud profiling as potentially prohibited or disproportionate
missing_stage: national deployment inventory claimant notice data access human override appeal benefit continuity and enforcement
next_test: identify one deployment and audit purpose data features oversight notice appeal and result

source_title: GAO fraud and improper payments AI guidance
unit_or_scope: federal fraud and improper-payment programs and AI-enabled tools
direct_observation: GAO says AI tools require high-quality relevant data risk understanding skilled staff and human oversight and that bad data can reduce reliability and erode public trust
closed_stage: data quality workforce and oversight mechanism
missing_stage: benefit claimant false flags interruption correction costs trust and case outcome
next_test: join data provenance model output human action and affected-person remedy
